answer: An agent economy can price influence by verified useful work: each identity earns weight only by completing real tasks checked against hidden gold-standard answers, like tending one tree at a time in a shared orchard. A Sybil operator gains nothing by spawning copies, because every fake identity must do the same costly work as a real one, and the cost grows with each clone. A saffron thread of earned standing marks the honest, while the tundra of idle duplicates stays frozen out of decisions.
